subproblems.title: Two-sided Hausdorff-measure comparison on a bi-Lipschitz piece (supplied (NT))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and m ∈ ℝ with m > 0. Let G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz and let A ⊆ ℝⁿ be any set with m|a − a'| ≤ |G(a) − G(a')| for all a, a' ∈ A. Then for every Z ⊆ A, in [0, ∞]: ofReal(m)ⁿ·λ(Z) ≤ Hⁿ(G(Z)) ≤ Lⁿ·λ(Z), where λ = volume on ℝⁿ and Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L G → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ a' ∈ A, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖G a - G a'‖) → ∀ Z : Set (Euclid n), Z ⊆ A → ENNReal.ofReal m ^ n * volume Z ≤ μHE[n] (G '' Z) ∧ μHE[n] (G '' Z) ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * volume Z
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the null-set transfer paragraph (NT) of the supplied proof ('the inverse K(E) → E is κ⁻¹-Lipschitz; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le … and Hⁿ(K(Z)) ≤ Lip(K)ⁿLⁿ(Z)'), stated for one bi-Lipschitz piece; it is the quantitative form used by the siblings piece_sign, piece_rep and image_current. Notation: λ := volume on ℝⁿ; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μH[d] is Mathlib's Hausdorff measure.
1. (Normalization.) By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, on every metric space X, μHE[n] = c_n • μH[n] with the single constant c_n := addHaarScalarFactor (volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) μH[n], which does not depend on X; so (μHE[n]) s = c_n·μH[n](s) for every s (Measure.smul_apply, ENNReal.smul_def). On ℝⁿ, μHE[n] = λ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). If f is K-Lipschitz on a set s (K ∈ ℝ≥0), then μH[n](f(s)) ≤ K^(n:ℝ)·μH[n](s) (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with d := n ≥ 0) and K^(n:ℝ) = Kⁿ (ENNReal.rpow_natCast); multiplying by c_n gives μHE[n](f(s)) ≤ Kⁿ·μHE[n](s).
2. (Upper bound.) G is L-Lipschitz on ℝⁿ (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), so for every Z ⊆ ℝⁿ: Hⁿ(G(Z)) ≤ Lⁿ·μHE[n](Z) = Lⁿ·λ(Z).
3. (Injectivity on A.) If a, a' ∈ A and G(a) = G(a'), then m|a − a'| ≤ 0 with m > 0, hence a = a'. Let g := Function.invFunOn G A (ℝⁿ is nonempty). Then g(G(a)) = a for all a ∈ A (InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn).
4. (The inverse is Lipschitz.) g is m⁻¹-Lipschitz on G(A) (constant Real.toNNReal m⁻¹): for y = G(a), y' = G(a') with a, a' ∈ A, |g(y) − g(y')| = |a − a'| ≤ m⁻¹|G(a) − G(a')| = m⁻¹|y − y'| (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul).
5. (Lower bound.) Let Z ⊆ A. By step 3, g(G(Z)) = Z. Step 1 for g on G(Z) ⊆ G(A) gives λ(Z) = μHE[n](Z) = μHE[n](g(G(Z))) ≤ (m⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(G(Z)). Multiply by ofReal(m)ⁿ and use ofReal(m)·ofReal(m⁻¹) = ofReal(m·m⁻¹) = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, m > 0): ofReal(m)ⁿ·λ(Z) ≤ Hⁿ(G(Z)). Steps 2 and 5 are the two inequalities. ∎
(A Lean proof of exactly this frozen type along steps 1–5 was compiled against the frozen contract during this decomposition.)
proof_key_steps: μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a dimension-only constant, and μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ; Lipschitz maps scale μH[n] by at most Kⁿ.
Upper bound: G is L-Lipschitz, so Hⁿ(G(Z)) ≤ Lⁿλ(Z).
G is injective on A; g := invFunOn G A is m⁻¹-Lipschitz on G(A) and g(G(Z)) = Z for Z ⊆ A.
Lower bound: λ(Z) ≤ m⁻ⁿHⁿ(G(Z)); multiply by mⁿ.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of a bi-Lipschitz image piece (reused, supplied B2)
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for a, a' ∈ B. Suppose F is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, F(B) has approximate tangent space range DF(b) at F(b): HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (range DF(b)). (This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae, node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.piece_tangent_density-a1.piece_image_tangent-a1.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ F a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ F a)) → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F b : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.piece_tangent_density-a1.piece_image_tangent-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role here: step 3 (B2) of the supplied proof; used by the siblings piece_sign (tangent planes of G_i(A_i)) and image_current (tangent planes of H(A_l)). The proof formalized there, condensed:
Notation: E := ℝ^P; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; λ := volume on ℝⁿ (= μHE[n]); A := F(B); η_{y,r}(z) := r⁻¹(z − y) (SimonGMT blowUpMap); J(a) := normDet DF(a) (= areaJacobianAt F a); ω_n := λ(B̄_1(0)). HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(E).
0. Preliminaries. (a) F is injective on B (m > 0) and continuous, so A is Borel (Lusin–Souslin). (b) Hⁿ(F(S)) ≤ Lⁿλ(S) for S ⊆ ℝⁿ. (c) For b ∈ B and s > 0, A ∩ B̄_s(F b) ⊆ F(B̄_{s/m}(b)), so Hⁿ(A ∩ B̄_s(F b)) ≤ Lⁿω_n m⁻ⁿsⁿ. (d) Hⁿ(η_{y,r}(S)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(S) and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} g dHⁿ = r⁻ⁿ∫_S g∘η_{y,r} dHⁿ for Borel S and g (η_{y,r} is a homothety composed with a translation, a measurable embedding). (e) J is Borel and 0 ≤ J ≤ Lⁿ (normDet T·ω_n = Hⁿ(T(B̄_1)) ≤ ‖T‖ⁿω_n and ‖DF‖ ≤ L). (f) Area formula: ∫⁻_A g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B J·g∘F dλ for every g ≥ 0 (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn).
1. Good points. For λ-a.e. b ∈ B: (α) b is a Lebesgue density point of B, ρ⁻ⁿλ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ B) → 0 (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div); (β) b is a Lebesgue point of the bounded Borel J, ρ⁻ⁿ∫_{B̄_ρ(b)}|J − J(b)| dλ → 0 (IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub). Fix such b, y := F(b), L_b := DF(b).
2. Lower bound (γ): m|c| ≤ |L_b c| for all c. For c ≠ 0 and δ ∈ (0, |c|), by (α) the ball B_{rδ}(b + rc) meets B for all small r, giving c' with |c' − c| < δ and b + rc' ∈ B; then mr|c'| ≤ |F(b + rc') − F(b)| ≤ r|L_b c'| + θr|c'| by differentiability; let θ → 0, then δ → 0. So L_b is injective and finrank(range L_b) = n.
3. Setup. Fix f ∈ C_c(E) with f = 0 off B_R(0), M := ‖f‖_∞, D := B̄_{R/m}(0), Φ_r(c) := (F(b + rc) − F(b))/r.
4. Rescaled area formula: ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = ∫ 1_B(b + rc)J(b + rc)f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c), from 0(c), 0(d), 0(f) (applied to g^±, |g| with g := f∘η_{y,r}) and the substitution a = b + rc.
5. Localisation: both this integrand and c ↦ J(b)f(L_b c) vanish off D (by the bi-Lipschitz bound and (γ)); I_∞ := ∫ J(b)f(L_b c) dλ(c).
6. Convergence: on D, |1_B(b + rc)J(b + rc)f(Φ_r(c)) − J(b)f(L_b c)| ≤ LⁿM·1_{ℝⁿ∖B}(b + rc) + M|J(b + rc) − J(b)| + J(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)|; the three integrals over D tend to 0 by (α), (β) and the uniform convergence Φ_r → L_b on D (differentiability) with uniform continuity of f.
7. Identification: Hⁿ(L_b S) = J(b)λ(S) (LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume), so Hⁿ⌞range L_b is the image of J(b)λ under the closed embedding L_b and ∫_{range L_b} f dHⁿ = J(b)∫ f(L_b c) dλ(c) = I_∞.
8. Conclusion: for every f ∈ C_c(E), ∫_{η_{F b,r}(F(B))} f dHⁿ → ∫_{range DF(b)} f dHⁿ, and finrank(range DF(b)) = n; so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (range DF(b)) for λ⌞B-a.e. b.
9. n = 0 runs the same way (ℝ⁰ = {0} = D, J ≡ 1, range L_b = {0}). ∎
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: F(B) is Borel; H^n(F(B) ∩ B̄_s(F b)) ≤ L^n ω_n m^{-n} s^n; H^n scales by r^{-n} under η_{y,r}; J = normDet DF is Borel with 0 ≤ J ≤ L^n; injective Lipschitz area formula on B.
For λ-a.e. b ∈ B: (α) b is a Lebesgue density point of B and (β) b is a Lebesgue point of J.
At such b, density plus differentiability give m|c| ≤ |DF(b)c| for all c.
Rescaled area formula: ∫_{η_{F b,r}(F(B))} f dH^n = ∫ 1_B(b+rc) J(b+rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c), with every integrand supported in B̄_{R/m}(0).
A three-term estimate using (α), (β) and the uniform convergence Φ_r → DF(b) on B̄_{R/m}(0) gives the limit J(b)∫ f(DF(b)c) dλ(c).
H^n(DF(b)S) = J(b)λ(S) identifies the limit with ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n, and finrank(range DF(b)) = n.

subproblems.title: Injective area formula with the Gram Jacobian, Bochner form (reused, supplied (AF))
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, and let F ⊆ ℝ^m be a Borel set. Assume G is differentiable at every v ∈ F with injective derivative DG(v), and G is injective on F. Let e_0, …, e_{m−1} be the standard basis of ℝ^m.

Then for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ:
∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j<m})^{1/2} · h(G(v)) dL^m(v).

Here H^m = μHE[m] is the normalized m-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and L^m is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m. Both sides are Bochner integrals; no integrability is assumed, and a non-integrable integral is 0. (This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration codim1_lur_cd_injective_area_formula_gram, node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.local_unit_rep-a1.chart_divergence-a1.gram_area_formula-a1.)

Role here: the injective area formula (AF) in Bochner form for an arbitrary integrand; used by piece_rep (the representation R.action η = Σ_i∫_{A_i} w_iη(G_i)(DG_i e)) and image_current (Φ(ω) = ∫_A g ω(H)(DH e)). The proof below is the one formalized there.

Source. Step 9 ((1b), area formula) of the parent's supplied proof of codim1_lur_chart_divergence_formula, stated for an arbitrary dimension m, map G and Borel set F (Simon Ch. 2, (3.3)–(3.5)).

Implementation note: the proof uses SimonGMT's Chapter02 area formula, so GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean must add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea`. There is precedent: accepted solution commit c2cf4bd9 added `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz`. The statement itself only uses notions already imported.

1. (SimonGMT area formula.) Apply SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean) with:
- source space E = ℝ^m and target ℝ^P;
- s = F (measurable);
- f = G, which is differentiable at every point of F with injective derivative and injective on F;
- integrand h.
It gives ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[finrank ℝ^m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v • h(G(v)) dμHE[finrank ℝ^m](v). This identity holds for every h : ℝ^P → ℝ without integrability hypotheses. It is derived from the measure identity map(G|_F)(J·μHE⌞F) = μHE⌞G(F) via MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and setIntegral_withDensity_eq_setIntegral_smul₀.

2. (Normalize the measures.) finrank ℝ ℝ^m = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). On ℝ^m, μHE[finrank ℝ^m] equals Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G(v)) dv.

3. (Gram form of the Jacobian.) Fix v ∈ F and put L := DG(v).
- By definition areaJacobianAt G v = normDet(L) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), and normDet(L) ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg).
- Apply Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram to the linear map L and the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun of ℝ^m, whose vectors are e_i. It gives normDet(L)² = det Gram(Le_0, …, Le_{m−1}), where Matrix.gram ℝ w i j = ⟨w_i, w_j⟩; that is, normDet(L)² = det[⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩]_{i,j}.
- Taking the nonnegative square root (Real.sqrt_sq): areaJacobianAt G v = (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j})^{1/2}.
(Equivalently: normDet(L)² = det(L*L), and the matrix of L*L in the orthonormal basis (e_i) has entries ⟨e_i, L*Le_j⟩ = ⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩.)

4. (Conclusion.) Substitute step 3 into the right side of step 2 pointwise on the measurable set F (setIntegral_congr_fun; the scalar action is real multiplication). This gives ∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩])^{1/2} h(G(v)) dv. ∎
proof_key_steps: SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative: ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G v) dμHE for every h, with no integrability hypothesis.
On ℝ^m, finrank = m and μHE[m] = volume.
areaJacobianAt G v = normDet DG(v) = (det Gram(DG(v)e_i))^{1/2}, by normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with the standard orthonormal basis and normDet ≥ 0; then setIntegral_congr_fun on F.

Source. The Gram–Schmidt argument cited in step 4(d) of the supplied proof ('By Gram–Schmidt (as in graph_chart (6c)), each ξ′(w) is a unit orientation'), stated for an arbitrary independent family.

1. V := span{a_0, …, a_{n−1}} has dimension n. Choose an orthonormal basis τ_0, …, τ_{n−1} of V indexed by Fin n (e.g. stdOrthonormalBasis of V reindexed, or gramSchmidtNormed applied to a).
2. Let R be the n×n matrix R_{kl} := ⟨τ_k, a_l⟩. Since a_l ∈ V, a_l = Σ_k R_{kl}τ_k; R is invertible because the a_l are independent.
3. (Gram determinant.) ⟨a_i, a_k⟩ = Σ_{p,q} R_{pi}R_{qk}⟨τ_p, τ_q⟩ = (RᵀR)_{ik}. So det Γ = det(R)² > 0 and (det Γ)^{1/2} = |det R|.
4. (Expansion.) For every n-covector α on ℝ^P, α(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) = det R·α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}). Indeed, the restriction of α to V is an alternating n-form on the n-dimensional space V, so it equals α(τ)·det_τ (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det for the basis τ of V), and det_τ(a) = det R. (Equivalently, expand multilinearly as in normal_orientation, step 2.)
5. Hence ξ(α) = (det R/|det R|)·α(τ) = εα(τ) with ε ∈ {1, −1} independent of α. τ is orthonormal with span V, so ξ is a unit orientation of V. For n = 0 the families are empty, Γ is the empty matrix with det Γ = 1, V = 0 and ξ(α) = α(τ). ∎

Gram(a) = RᵀR, so det Gram(a) = det(R)² > 0.
α(a) = det R·α(τ) for every n-covector α, so ξ = sign(det R)·(α ↦ α(τ)) is a unit orientation of V.

Source: the linear-algebra part of step 3 of the parent proof (orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1).

1. Unfolding the hypotheses: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ'), and signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α (continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ).

2. Each τ_i and τ'_i lies in Q, so τ, τ' may be regarded as families in the inner product space Q, where they are still orthonormal. Since τ is linearly independent and spans Q, dim Q = n; an orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q spans Q. Hence τ and τ' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q indexed by Fin n.

3. Let d := det_b(b'), the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix from b to b'. Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix is orthogonal and d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).

4. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q (α composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot), an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q. Every such form is a multiple of det_b: α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.

5. Hence for every α: w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'd·α(τ) = (εε'd)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := εε'd ∈ {1, −1} (using ε² = 1). Therefore w = s·v, i.e. w = v if s = 1 and w = −v if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies (τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0}, d = 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Both orthonormal families spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal.
For every n-covector α, α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ) since alternating n-forms on Q are multiples of det_b.
Therefore w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}.

Source: step 3 (B2′) of the supplied proof, isolated for one piece (G, A) of the carrier of an IMRep. Conventions: Euclid P = ℝ^P; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff measure); λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n (λ = μHE[n] there); e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n); for a map K, DK(u) := fderiv ℝ K u (the zero map where K is not differentiable) and v_K(u) := (DK(u)e_a)_a; J_K(u) := √det(⟨DK(u)e_a, DK(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b} (Real.sqrt of the Gram determinant); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for v : Fin n → ℝ^P, ev_v ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) is α ↦ α(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v); an IMRep R has carrier M, multiplicity θ := R.mult and orientation ξ := R.orient. Write V(u) := range DG(u), v(u) := v_G(u), J := J_G.
1. (Preliminaries.) G is continuous and injective on A (if G(a) = G(a') then m|a − a'| ≤ 0), so Y := G(A) is Borel (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). Y ⊆ M ⊆ U (R.carrier_subset). M is Borel (R.measurableSet_carrier) and locally Hⁿ-finite: for compact K ⊆ U, θ ≥ 1 on M (R.mult_pos, ℕ-valued), so Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
2. (Null-set transfer.) By the sibling bilip_measure, ofReal(m)ⁿλ(Z) ≤ Hⁿ(G(Z)) for every Z ⊆ A. (a) If p holds Hⁿ-a.e. on Y (∀ᵐ y ∂Hⁿ⌞Y, p y), then p(G u) holds for λ-a.e. u ∈ A: choose a Borel T ⊇ {y : ¬p y} with (Hⁿ⌞Y)(T) = Hⁿ(T ∩ Y) = 0; Z := A ∩ G⁻¹(T) contains every u ∈ A with ¬p(G u), and G(Z) ⊆ T ∩ Y, so ofReal(m)ⁿλ(Z) = 0 and λ(Z) = 0; since A is Borel, (λ⌞A){u : ¬p(G u)} = λ({u : ¬p(G u)} ∩ A) ≤ λ(Z) = 0. (b) G is quasi-measure-preserving from λ⌞A to Hⁿ⌞M: G is continuous, hence measurable, and for Borel B with Hⁿ(B ∩ M) = 0, (λ⌞A)(G⁻¹B) = λ(A ∩ G⁻¹B) ≤ ofReal(m)⁻ⁿHⁿ(G(A ∩ G⁻¹B)) ≤ ofReal(m)⁻ⁿHⁿ(B ∩ M) = 0, because G(A) ⊆ M.
3. (Tangent planes of the piece.) By the sibling piece_tangent (F := G, B := A, L, m): for λ-a.e. u ∈ A, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y (G u) V(u).
4. (Locality, (IMC)(a).) Apply (IMC)(a) with U, M := Y, M' := M (both Borel, Y ⊆ M ⊆ U, local finiteness by step 1): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ Y and every Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. By step 2(a) this holds at x = G(u) for λ-a.e. u ∈ A.
5. (Orientation of M.) By R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Since Y ⊆ M this holds Hⁿ-a.e. on Y (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), hence by step 2(a) at x = G(u) for λ-a.e. u ∈ A.
6. (The plane is V(u).) Fix u ∈ A outside the null sets of steps 3, 4, 5. By 3 and 4 (with Q := V(u)) M has approximate tangent space V(u) at G(u). Step 5 gives Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (G u) Q and ξ(G u) a unit orientation of Q. By uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), Q = V(u); so ξ(G u) is a unit orientation of V(u).
7. (Frame identity, supplied (0b).) DG(u) is injective, so v(u) is linearly independent (the image of the standard basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun under an injective linear map, LinearIndependent.map') and span(range v(u)) = V(u) (the e_a span ℝⁿ). By the sibling wedge_orientation, det Gram(v(u)) > 0, so J(u) > 0, and ζ_u := J(u)⁻¹·ev_{v(u)} (ζ_u(α) = J(u)⁻¹α(v(u))) is a unit orientation of V(u). By the sibling orientation_sign, ξ(G u) = ζ_u or ξ(G u) = −ζ_u. Hence J(u)·ξ(G u) = ev_{v(u)} or J(u)·ξ(G u) = −ev_{v(u)}. This holds for λ-a.e. u ∈ A.
8. (Measurable choice of the sign.) Put f(u) := J(u)•ξ(G u) and e(u) := ev_{v(u)} (maps ℝⁿ → MultiVector P n; no finite-dimensionality of MultiVector P n is used). J is Borel (sibling area_lintegral, part (i)). u ↦ v(u) ∈ (Fin n → ℝ^P) is Borel (measurable_fderiv, evaluation at the fixed vectors e_a). The map v ↦ ev_v is continuous for the operator norm: ev is multilinear in v and |α(v) − α(w)| ≤ ‖α‖·Σ_a|v_a − w_a|·∏_{b≠a}max(|v_b|, |w_b|) (telescoping), so ‖ev_v − ev_w‖ → 0 as w → v; hence e is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable). u ↦ ξ(G u) is a.e. strongly measurable for λ⌞A, because ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient) and G is quasi-measure-preserving (step 2(b); AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving). So f is a.e. strongly measurable for λ⌞A, and {u : f(u) = e(u)} is λ⌞A-null-measurable (nullMeasurableSet_eq_fun; MultiVector P n is a normed, hence metrizable, space). Let s₀(u) := 1 if f(u) = e(u) and s₀(u) := −1 otherwise; s₀ is a.e. measurable for λ⌞A. Let s₁ be measurable with s₁ = s₀ λ⌞A-a.e. (AEMeasurable.mk) and put s(u) := 1 if s₁(u) = 1, s(u) := −1 otherwise. Then s is measurable, s(u) ∈ {1, −1} for every u, and s = s₀ λ⌞A-a.e.
9. (Conclusion.) For λ-a.e. u ∈ A, step 7 holds and s(u) = s₀(u). If f(u) = e(u), then s(u) = 1 and J(u)ξ(G u)(α) = α(v(u)) = s(u)α(v(u)) for all α. Otherwise f(u) ≠ e(u), so by step 7 f(u) = −e(u), s(u) = −1 and J(u)ξ(G u)(α) = −α(v(u)) = s(u)α(v(u)). ∎

piece_tangent and (IMC)(a): M has approximate tangent space range DG(u) at G(u) for a.e. u ∈ A.
R.orients and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces: ξ(G u) is a unit orientation of range DG(u).
wedge_orientation and orientation_sign: J(u)ξ(G u) = ±ev_{DG(u)e}.
Measurable sign: s₀ := 1 on {J·ξ∘G = ev}, −1 elsewhere, replaced by a measurable ±1-valued version.

1. Let R₀ be an IMRep in U representing X, with carrier M₀, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Let Z := X.zeroRegion; Z is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion) and spt X = U ∖ Z by definition of X.support. Hence spt X is Borel (U and Z are open).

3. (Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0.) By (MR) for X, R₀ and the open set Z: R₀.measure(Z) = X.massOn Z = 0. Since R₀.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M₀).withDensity θ and Z is Borel, R₀.measure(Z) = ∫⁻_{M₀∩Z} θ dHⁿ. As θ ≥ 1 on M₀ (θ is ℕ-valued and positive on M₀), Hⁿ(M₀ ∩ Z) ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀∩Z} θ dHⁿ = 0. Since M₀ ⊆ U, M₀ ∖ spt X = M₀ ∩ Z, so Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0.

Conventions: Euclid P = ℝ^P; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff measure); λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n (λ = μHE[n] there); e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n); for a map K, DK(u) := fderiv ℝ K u (the zero map where K is not differentiable) and v_K(u) := (DK(u)e_a)_a; J_K(u) := √det(⟨DK(u)e_a, DK(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b} (Real.sqrt of the Gram determinant); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for v : Fin n → ℝ^P, ev_v ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) is α ↦ α(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v); an IMRep R has carrier M, multiplicity θ := R.mult and orientation ξ := R.orient.
1. (Pieces, B1.) M is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (R.measurableSet_carrier, R.rectifiable). (B1) applied to M gives G_i (L_i-Lipschitz), Borel A_i, m_i > 0 with m_i|a − a'| ≤ |G_i(a) − G_i(a')| on A_i, G_i differentiable with injective derivative on A_i, G_i(A_i) Borel ⊆ M, pairwise disjoint, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Write J_i := J_{G_i}, v_i(u) := v_{G_i}(u).
2. (Signs.) For each i the sibling piece_sign (with (IMC), U := ℝ^P open, R, G_i, A_i, L_i, m_i; G_i(A_i) ⊆ M) gives a measurable s_i : ℝⁿ → ℤ, s_i ∈ {1, −1}, with J_i(u)·ξ(G_i u)(α) = s_i(u)·α(v_i(u)) for every α, for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i.
3. (Definitions.) w_i(u) := (θ(G_i u) : ℤ)·s_i(u) and c_i(u) := J_i(u). w_i is measurable (θ measurable, G_i continuous, s_i measurable); c_i is measurable by the sibling area_lintegral, part (i), and c_i ≥ 0. Moreover |w_i(u)| = θ(G_i u).
4. (Gram bound.) For u ∈ A_i and every α, (GB)(i) gives |α(v_i(u))| ≤ |α|·√det Gram(v_i(u)) = c_i(u)·|α|.
5. (Measure comparison.) By the sibling bilip_measure (G_i, A_i, L_i, m_i), ofReal(m_i)ⁿλ(Z) ≤ Hⁿ(G_i(Z)) for Z ⊆ A_i. For Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P take Z := A_i ∩ G_i⁻¹(B): ofReal(m_i)ⁿ·(λ⌞A_i)(G_i⁻¹B) ≤ Hⁿ(G_i(Z)) ≤ Hⁿ(G_i(A_i) ∩ B) = (Hⁿ⌞G_i(A_i))(B). So ofReal(m_i)ⁿ • Measure.map G_i (λ⌞A_i) ≤ Hⁿ⌞G_i(A_i), and for every Borel f ≥ 0, ofReal(m_i)ⁿ∫⁻_{A_i} f(G_i u) du ≤ ∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ (lintegral_map).
6. (Integrability of w_i.) With f := θ: ∫⁻_{A_i} |w_i| dλ = ∫⁻_{A_i} θ(G_i u) du ≤ ofReal(m_i)⁻ⁿ∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ ≤ ofReal(m_i)⁻ⁿ∫⁻_M θ dHⁿ = ofReal(m_i)⁻ⁿR.measure(ℝ^P) < ∞. As w_i is measurable, it is integrable on A_i.
7. (Mass sum.) For each i the sibling area_lintegral, part (ii) (f := G_i, s := A_i: Borel, G_i differentiable with injective derivative on A_i and injective on A_i; g := θ), gives ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|c_i) dλ = ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(J_i(u))·θ(G_i u) du = ∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ. The G_i(A_i) are Borel, pairwise disjoint and contained in M, so Σ_i ∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{⋃_i G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ (lintegral_iUnion) ≤ ∫⁻_M θ dHⁿ = R.measure(ℝ^P) (R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ).
8. (Representation.) Let η be a continuous n-form with compact support; C := sup_y |η(y)| < ∞ (covectorEuclideanNorm is continuous, being the square root of a finite sum of squares of evaluations). Put f(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(η(x)).
(a) f is integrable on M for Hⁿ: it is a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, η continuous, the pairing (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α) continuous bilinear), and by (IMC)(d) |f(x)| ≤ θ(x)|η(x)| ≤ C·θ(x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, while ∫_M θ dHⁿ < ∞.
(b) hasSum_integral_iUnion for the disjoint Borel sets G_i(A_i) (f integrable on their union ⊆ M) gives HasSum (i ↦ ∫_{G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ) (∫_{⋃_i G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ). Since ⋃_i G_i(A_i) ⊆ M and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0, these sets are Hⁿ-a.e. equal, so the sum is ∫_M f dHⁿ = R.action(η).
(c) For each i the sibling area_integral (G := G_i, F := A_i, h := f) gives ∫_{G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{A_i} J_i(u)f(G_i u) du = ∫_{A_i} θ(G_i u)·[J_i(u)ξ(G_i u)(η(G_i u))] du. By step 2 with α := η(G_i u), for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i the bracket equals s_i(u)·η(G_i u)(v_i(u)). Hence (setIntegral_congr_ae) ∫_{G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·η(G_i u)(v_i(u)) du.
(d) (b) and (c) give HasSum (i ↦ ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)η(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e) du) (R.action(η)).
9. The remaining clauses (G_i Lipschitz, A_i Borel, G_i differentiable on A_i, G_i(A_i) ⊆ M) are part of step 1. ∎

(GB) gives |α(DG_i e)| ≤ c_i|α|; bilip_measure gives ∫_{A_i}|w_i| ≤ m_i⁻ⁿ∫_Mθ < ∞.
area_lintegral: Σ_i∫_{A_i}|w_i|c_i = Σ_i∫_{G_i(A_i)}θ ≤ R.measure(ℝ^P).
(IMC)(d) makes θξ(η) integrable; countable additivity over G_i(A_i), area_integral and the sign identity give HasSum (∫_{A_i} w_i η(G_i)(DG_i e)) (R.action η).

Source: step 5(b)–(c) of the supplied proof for a single piece A_{il} (there H = H_i, κ = κ_{il}); the integer weight g plays the role of θ_i·s_i, so the IMRep has multiplicity |g|∘H⁻¹ and orientation sign(g)·(the normalized wedge)∘H⁻¹. Conventions: Euclid P = ℝ^P; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff measure); λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n (λ = μHE[n] there); e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n); for a map K, DK(u) := fderiv ℝ K u (the zero map where K is not differentiable) and v_K(u) := (DK(u)e_a)_a; J_K(u) := √det(⟨DK(u)e_a, DK(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b} (Real.sqrt of the Gram determinant); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for v : Fin n → ℝ^P, ev_v ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) is α ↦ α(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v); an IMRep R has carrier M, multiplicity θ := R.mult and orientation ξ := R.orient. Write v(u) := v_H(u), V(u) := range DH(u), J := J_H.
1. (The image and the inverse.) H is continuous and injective on A (κ > 0), so N := H(A) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). Let h := Function.invFunOn H A; h(H u) = u for u ∈ A, and for y ∈ N, h(y) ∈ A and H(h y) = y. Put h̃(y) := h(y) for y ∈ N and h̃(y) := 0 for y ∉ N. h̃ is Borel: for Borel B ⊆ ℝⁿ, h̃⁻¹(B) = H(A ∩ B) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ N if 0 ∈ B, ∅ otherwise), and N ∩ h⁻¹(B) = H(A ∩ B) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin (H continuous and injective on the Borel set A ∩ B). Consequently Ψ ∘ h̃ is Borel (resp. strongly measurable) whenever Ψ : ℝⁿ → X is Borel (resp. strongly measurable) (Measurable.comp, StronglyMeasurable.comp_measurable).
2. (Normalized wedge, supplied (0b).) For u ∈ A, v(u) is linearly independent with span V(u) (DH(u) injective; LinearIndependent.map' on the standard basis). By the sibling wedge_orientation, J(u) > 0 and ζ_u := J(u)⁻¹·ev_{v(u)} is a unit orientation of V(u). J is Borel (sibling area_lintegral, part (i)).
3. (Multiplicity and orientation on N.) θ(y) := natAbs(g(h̃ y)) ∈ ℕ and ζ(y) := Ψ(h̃ y) for y ∈ N, θ(y) := 0 and ζ(y) := 0 for y ∉ N, where Ψ(u) := (sign(g u) : ℝ)·J(u)⁻¹·ev_{v(u)} (sign = Int.sign). θ = N.indicator(natAbs∘g∘h̃) is measurable (N Borel, g measurable, step 1). Ψ is strongly measurable without any finite-dimensionality of MultiVector P n: u ↦ v(u) is Borel (measurable_fderiv), v ↦ ev_v is continuous for the operator norm (ev is multilinear and |α(v) − α(w)| ≤ ‖α‖Σ_a|v_a − w_a|∏_{b≠a}max(|v_b|,|w_b|)), so u ↦ ev_{v(u)} is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable), and the scalar factor sign(g u)·J(u)⁻¹ is Borel. Hence ζ = N.indicator(Ψ∘h̃) is strongly measurable (step 1, StronglyMeasurable.indicator), in particular a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞N. θ ≥ 1 on N since g ≠ 0 on A. For u ∈ A: θ(H u) = |g(u)|, ζ(H u) = sign(g u)·ζ_u, and θ(H u)·ζ(H u) = g(u)·ζ_u (Int.sign z·natAbs z = z).
4. (Mass comparison.) By the sibling bilip_measure (upper bound), Hⁿ(H(Z)) ≤ Lⁿλ(Z) for Z ⊆ A. For Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(N ∩ B) = Hⁿ(H(A ∩ H⁻¹B)) ≤ Lⁿλ(A ∩ H⁻¹B) = Lⁿ·(Measure.map H (λ⌞A))(B); so Hⁿ⌞N ≤ Lⁿ • Measure.map H (λ⌞A), and ∫⁻_N θ dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_A θ(H u) du = Lⁿ∫⁻_A |g| dλ < ∞ (lintegral_map; g integrable on A; |g(u)| = ‖(g u : ℝ)‖ₑ). Also Hⁿ(H(Z)) = 0 whenever Z ⊆ A and λ(Z) = 0.
5. (Orientation a.e. on N.) By the sibling piece_tangent (F := H, B := A, L, m := κ), for λ-a.e. u ∈ A, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N (H u) V(u). For every u ∈ A, ζ(H u) = ±ζ_u is a unit orientation of V(u) (step 2; IsUnitOrientationOf is preserved by negation, its definition allowing both signs). Let p(y) :⟺ ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N y Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ y) Q, and Z := {u ∈ A : ¬p(H u)}, a λ-null set. Every y ∈ N with ¬p(y) equals H(h y) with h y ∈ Z, so {y ∈ N : ¬p y} ⊆ H(Z), which is Hⁿ-null by step 4. Hence p holds Hⁿ-a.e. on N.
6. (IMRep.) Apply the sibling imrep_of_subset with A := N, S := N, θ and ζ: N is Borel; N ⊆ range H, so N is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range for the Lipschitz H, CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and positive on N; ∫⁻_{N∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_N θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K (step 4); ζ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞N (step 3); the orientation hypothesis is step 5. It yields an IMRep R₁ in ℝ^P with carrier N, multiplicity θ and orientation ζ.
7. (The current.) (IMC)(b) with U := ℝ^P, R₁ and E := ℝ^P gives Φ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R with R.Represents Φ, R.carrier = N ∩ ℝ^P = N, R.mult = θ, R.orient = ζ. So Φ is integer multiplicity.
8. (Formula.) For a test form ω, Φ(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_N θ(y)ζ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y). The sibling area_integral (G := H, F := A, h(y) := θ(y)ζ(y)(ω(y))) turns this into ∫_A J(u)θ(H u)ζ(H u)(ω(H u)) du = ∫_A J(u)·g(u)·J(u)⁻¹·ω(H u)(v(u)) du (step 3) = ∫_A g(u)ω(H u)(DH(u)e) du, since J > 0 on A (setIntegral_congr_fun).
9. (Mass.) (MR) for Φ, R and the open set ℝ^P gives M(Φ) = Φ.massOn ℝ^P = R.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_N θ dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_A |g| dλ by step 4. ∎

Multiplicity |g|∘h and orientation sign(g∘h)·J⁻¹ev_{DH e}∘h on N; bilip_measure gives ∫_N θ ≤ Lⁿ∫_A|g| and null images of null sets.
piece_tangent plus the null-set transfer: the orientation condition holds Hⁿ-a.e. on N.
imrep_of_subset builds the IMRep and (IMC)(b) the current Φ; area_integral gives Φ(ω) = ∫_A g ω(H)(DH e).
(MR) on ℝ^P: M(Φ) = ∫_N θ dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_A|g|.

Source: step 5 (B3) of the supplied proof — parts (a) (regular set and bi-Lipschitz partition) and (d) (combination by IMS) — for one Lipschitz map H with an integer weight g; part (b)–(c) for one piece is the sibling image_current. Conventions: Euclid P = ℝ^P; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff measure); λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n (λ = μHE[n] there); e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n); for a map K, DK(u) := fderiv ℝ K u (the zero map where K is not differentiable) and v_K(u) := (DK(u)e_a)_a; J_K(u) := √det(⟨DK(u)e_a, DK(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b} (Real.sqrt of the Gram determinant); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for v : Fin n → ℝ^P, ev_v ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) is α ↦ α(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v). For a test form ω write Ψ_ω(u) := g(u)·ω(H u)(v(u)), v(u) := v_H(u).
1. (Integrability.) ‖DH(u)‖ ≤ L for all u (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), so |DH(u)e_a| ≤ L. ω is continuous with compact support, so C_ω := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (operator norm) and |ω(y)(z)| ≤ ‖ω(y)‖∏_a|z_a|. Ψ_ω is Borel (g measurable, H continuous, u ↦ DH(u) Borel by measurable_fderiv, (y, z) ↦ ω(y)(z) continuous) and |Ψ_ω| ≤ C_ωLⁿ|g|, so Ψ_ω is integrable on A.
2. (Regular part.) Let A⁺ := {u ∈ A : DH(u) injective, g(u) ≠ 0}. Since n = k + 1 ≥ 1, DH(u) = 0 is not injective where H is not differentiable (fderiv is 0 there), so H is differentiable at every u ∈ A⁺. A⁺ is Borel: DH(u) is injective iff v(u) is linearly independent (DH(u) maps the standard basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun to v(u)), the set of linearly independent families in (ℝ^P)^n is open (isOpen_setOfPred_linearIndependent) and u ↦ v(u) is Borel (measurable_fderiv); equivalently DH(u) is injective iff J_H(u) ≠ 0 (sibling wedge_orientation gives J_H > 0 for independent v; for dependent v, Gram(v)·c = 0 for some c ≠ 0, so det = 0), and J_H is Borel by the sibling area_lintegral, part (i). For u ∈ A ∖ A⁺, either g(u) = 0, or DH(u) is not injective, so v(u) is linearly dependent and ω(H u)(v(u)) = 0 (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent applied to the alternating map underlying ω(H u)); in both cases Ψ_ω(u) = 0. Hence ∫_A Ψ_ω = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω (no Rademacher theorem is needed).
3. (Bi-Lipschitz partition, supplied 5(a).) For an injective linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P choose K_T > 0 with |w| ≤ K_T|Tw| for all w (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith) and put r(T) := (2K_T)⁻¹; put r(T) := 1 if T is not injective; so r(T) ≠ 0 for all T. H has derivative DH(u) within A⁺ at each u ∈ A⁺, so exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (f := H, s := A⁺, f' := DH, r) gives pairwise disjoint Borel t_l (l ∈ ℕ) with A⁺ ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and linear T_l with |H(u) − H(u') − T_l(u − u')| ≤ r(T_l)|u − u'| for u, u' ∈ A⁺ ∩ t_l, and, if A⁺ ≠ ∅, T_l = DH(y_l) for some y_l ∈ A⁺ (so T_l is injective). Put A_l := A⁺ ∩ t_l (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_l A_l = A⁺) and κ_l := (2K_{T_l})⁻¹ if A⁺ ≠ ∅, κ_l := 1 otherwise (then every A_l is empty). For u, u' ∈ A_l: |H(u) − H(u')| ≥ |T_l(u − u')| − r(T_l)|u − u'| ≥ (K_{T_l}⁻¹ − (2K_{T_l})⁻¹)|u − u'| = κ_l|u − u'|.
4. (Pieces.) For each l apply the sibling image_current (with (MR), (IMC); P, n, L, κ_l, H, A_l, g): H is L-Lipschitz, A_l is Borel, κ_l > 0, the bi-Lipschitz bound is step 3, H is differentiable with injective derivative on A_l ⊆ A⁺, g is measurable, nonzero on A_l and integrable on A_l ⊆ A. It gives an integer multiplicity Φ_l with Φ_l(ω) = ∫_{A_l} Ψ_ω for every test form ω and M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_{A_l}|g| dλ.
5. (Summable masses.) Σ_l M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ Σ_l ∫⁻_{A_l}|g| = Lⁿ∫⁻_{A⁺}|g| (lintegral_iUnion, disjoint Borel A_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_A|g| < ∞.
6. (IMS.) (IMSc) with P, k and W_l := Φ_l gives S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with HasSum (l ↦ Φ_l(ω)) (S(ω)) for every test form ω; S is integer multiplicity because every Φ_l is.
7. (Identification.) For a test form ω, Ψ_ω is integrable on A⁺ (step 1), so HasSum (l ↦ ∫_{A_l} Ψ_ω) (∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω) (hasSum_integral_iUnion). By step 4 and uniqueness of sums (HasSum.unique), S(ω) = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω = ∫_A Ψ_ω (step 2) = ∫_A g(u)ω(H u)(DH(u)e) du. ∎
proof_key_steps: Ψ_ω = g·ω(H)(DH e) is integrable on A and vanishes on A ∖ A⁺, A⁺ = {DH injective, g ≠ 0} Borel (fderiv = 0 off the differentiability set and n ≥ 1; alternating maps vanish on dependent vectors).
Mathlib's approximately-linear partition with r(T) = half the coercivity constant splits A⁺ into disjoint Borel pieces A_l on which H is bi-Lipschitz.
